newsitem.title: UK: UK's Shire buys U.S. Richwood Pharma.
newsitem.headline: UK's Shire buys U.S. Richwood Pharma.

text.p: Britain's Shire Pharmaceuticals Plc said on Monday it would buy Richwood Pharmaceutical Co Inc, a U.S. company specialising in drugs to treat central nervous system disorders.
Shire said it would initially pay up to $185.7 million for Richwood, which has annual sales of $15.3 million, and the merged group would be renamed Shire Richwood Inc.

Shire said Richwood focused on treatments for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), which affects between three and five percent of all children. Less than half are currently treated for the condition, the company said.
Shire said Richwood had two products --Adderall and Dextrosat -- competing in a market worth $457 million last year.
Shire said Adderall, approved last year by the Food and Drug Administration, had five percent of the market in the five months to May this year.
Shire said the initial price for Richwood would comprise $145.8 million of consideration shares, up to $15 million in cash and options over 7.2 million ordinary shares valued at $24.9 million.
